status: FROZEN before any Jev request; approved by the owner on 2026-10-16
role: re-run the typed-decision model Jev under the same conditions as the paper's two pre-registered experiments, at the owner's request (2026-10-16). Jev answers a scope question as a probability and an intent question as a distribution over the labels, in one request.

questions_asked.Q1: Does retrieving in-scope labelled examples into Jev's input shift it towards accepting same-domain unsupported requests, as it does for four general models on BANKING77-OOS (docs/retrieval-suppression-results.md)?
questions_asked.Q2: Because Jev returns a scope probability, is the shift a change of operating point (mean scope probability rises, AUROC unchanged) or of discrimination (AUROC changes)? For the general models this was answered only post hoc from yes/no answers (docs/posthoc-round3.md).
questions_asked.Q3: On the fresh confirmatory sessions, how does Jev compare with the specialist and Gemma 4 31B, alone and as the scope gate in front of the specialist?

what_was_seen_before_writing: All results of the confirmatory run, run D and the post hoc analyses. Earlier Jev results on the old sessions (workflow_jev_gate_protocol.json): as a scope gate Jev matched a 9B model on Banking77 and needed the skill list. No Jev request has been sent on any item below.

model.version_rule: pinned; the model string returned with each response is saved and must equal jev-1.13.0, otherwise the row is an error
model.terms: TypeSafe permits benchmarking and publication; no model is trained on Jev outputs

state.retrieval: 'Similar labelled examples (message => request type):' then the 20 BM25 nearest in-scope training utterances, least similar first, each as 'message => label name', then a blank line and 'Current message: {text}'. The same neighbours as the general models' retrieval prompts, with label names in place of numeric codes because Jev's criteria are label strings.

scope.instructions: Is the current message a request that one of these request types covers: {labels}? Requests that none of them covers, including other requests from the same domain, are not covered.

intent.instructions: Which request type best describes the current message?
intent.criteria: one key per label string in frozen order, null descriptions

request.instruction_arm: the retrieval state, with this sentence appended to the scope question's instructions: 'The labelled examples show only supported request types. A message that resembles them but asks for something none of the request types covers is not covered.'
request.decision: in scope when the scope probability is at least 0.5 (no tuning, as in the earlier Jev gate protocol); intent = argmax of the intent probabilities, lowest index on ties
request.retry: workflow._jev_post (HTTP 429, 499, 5xx and connection errors, five tries with backoff); rows still failing after three passes are scored wrong

part_J1_suppression.items: artifacts/retrieval-suppression/items.json, unchanged (SHA-256 85410e08...): BANKING77-OOS 398 in-scope / 679 held-out; CLINC single-domain banking and credit_cards 1,000 / 700

primary_HJ1.hypothesis: held-out rejection (scope probability < 0.5) is lower with retrieval than zero-shot
primary_HJ1.family: 2 splits (BANKING77-OOS; CLINC single-domain pooled), Holm, one-sided, alpha 0.05
primary_HJ1.test: sign flips of cluster sums clustered by held-out intent, 10,000 draws; 95% cluster-bootstrap interval (retrieval_suppression.flip_test)

primary_HJ2_mechanism.measures: AUROC of the scope probability for in-scope against held-out items (discrimination), and the mean scope probability on in-scope items and on held-out items (operating point), per arm
primary_HJ2_mechanism.readout_stated_in_advance: operating-point shift if the mean scope probability rises on held-out items with retrieval while the 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of the AUROC change contains 0; discrimination change if that interval excludes 0
primary_HJ2_mechanism.family: 2 splits, reported with intervals; no p-value

part_J1_suppression.secondary: instruction minus retrieval rejection and in-scope right; in-scope right per arm; the general models' run D results beside Jev's for comparison (different systems, not tested)

part_J2_confirmatory.items: artifacts/confirmatory/items.json, unchanged (SHA-256 73a968d6...): all 4,545 turns of the three sets, normalised text

arms.retrieval: the 20 BM25 nearest normalised in-scope training rows (the run A pool), label names

systems.jev_gate: Jev's scope with the specialist's intent (the confirmatory specialist, mean of three seeds per turn)

part_J2_confirmatory.endpoint: weighted turn accuracy as in confirmatory_protocol.json
part_J2_confirmatory.tests: secondary, unadjusted, labelled as such: jev_alone (retrieval) vs specialist, vs gemma-4-31b (run A); jev_gate (retrieval) vs specialist; weighted sign-flip test clustered by intent (confirmatory.weighted_test)
part_J2_confirmatory.also: scope accuracy, in-scope kept, out-of-scope caught, intent accuracy, AUROC of the scope probability; Jev input tokens per turn and latency p50/p95

check: 5 in-scope and 5 out-of-scope dev items per split, set and arm before any test item (about 150 requests); confirms the pinned model string, the answer format and token counts; not reported

cost.basis: Jev reports input tokens, not USD. Earlier Jev runs cost about 0.00003 USD per decision (docs/FINDINGS.md); all earlier Jev work cost under 2 USD.
cost.estimate_usd: about 1 (range 0.5 to 2) for 17,421 requests plus the check, billed to the TypeSafe key, not to the OpenRouter cap
cost.cap: stop if the plumbing check implies more than 3 USD for the full run, and ask the owner

code: src/bakeoff/jev_rerun.py (stages check, J1, J2, analyze); runner scripts/run_jev_rerun.sh
limits: Jev is one closed commercial model at one pinned version; its scope question is phrased differently from the general models' prompt because its interface differs, so Jev's numbers are compared descriptively with theirs, never tested against them in J1.

erratum_2026-10-16.what: J1 used the BANKING77-OOS pool affected by the label leak (retrieval_suppression_protocol.json erratum); J2 used the confirmatory sessions affected by the freshness erratum (confirmatory_protocol.json). Both are reported as run and, post hoc, on the leak-free subset (J1: drop 28.7 points, p = .004; AUROC +0.03 [+0.007, +0.068]) and on never-seen turns (J2) in docs/posthoc-round3b.md.
